In this World Cup finals, over 23%, nearly a quarter of the players were not born in the country they represent, with both the proportion and number reaching an all-time high. Among the 48 teams, eight squads have a majority of players born outside the country. The Netherlands' constituent country in the Caribbean, Curaçao, whose population is even smaller than that of Wan Chai, has only its most valuable player, Sheffield United's Guangdong descendant Tahith Chong, born locally, while all other players come from the Netherlands proper. Trailing only Curaçao and the Democratic Republic of Congo, the African "top dog" Morocco, which has the third-highest number of foreign-born players, even set a World Cup record in its opening group match against Brazil, with all 11 players on the pitch not born in the country it represents.

The contradiction of strong versus weak matchups at the World Cup is not only reflected in the fans' viewing perspective, but also in FIFA's struggle to simultaneously boost attention through both big-name stars and obscure small nations. The numerous controversies in this tournament, coupled with fans mocking star players being promoted as "FIFA Boys," as well as multiple team representatives submitting complaints to FIFA about refereeing standards after matches, reflect that while FIFA has set new revenue records at this World Cup, the most important participants in the game—the players themselves—are seeing their confidence in the conflict-ridden host organization plummet to a new low.

For fans, when recalling the classic matches of the 2026 World Cup in the future, it may not be the final, but perhaps the round-of-16 match where defending champions Argentina edged Cape Verde 3-2. The previously unknown 40-year-old Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha (禾仙夏), who consecutively saved shots from football king Lionel Messi, became famous overnight and is now a globally recognized player with nearly 30 million followers. For players born in small nations, being able to compete on equal terms with legendary stars on the world's biggest sporting stage through sheer ability is the true charm of the World Cup. Cape Verde defender Lopes, who nearly missed his call-up, said after the match: "One of the best things that happened at this World Cup is that no one asks anymore where Cape Verde is on the map. For us, this is making history. We have already put ourselves on the map."

考慮將參賽球隊增至 64 隊

On the eve of the previous World Cup, FIFA wrote to all participating teams, earnestly requesting "let football be the protagonist," and not allow football to be drawn into any ideological or political struggles. At that time, the World Cup was still hosted by a single country and featured 32 national teams. The next World Cup will celebrate its centenary and will be hosted across three continents and six countries in unprecedented fashion. Amid the controversies, as this World Cup enters its final stretch, President Gianni Infantino stated that he would consider expanding the number of participating teams to 64, describing the World Cup as "belonging to the whole world" (for the whole world). In a changing world, the saying that "the ball is round" has ignited unprecedented hope for global audiences once every four years, but only in a fair competition environment can victory truly belong to football and to you.
